Opened 2026-10-08: City of Pasadena (Texas) City Council record of proceedings, regular meeting of January 7, 2025: public hearing 'on the extension of the Commercial Moratorium imposed by the City of Pasadena, Texas, on the issuance of permits for the placement and installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) Facilities', then 'ORDINANCE 2025-001 - Authorizing and approving the Extension of the Commercial Moratorium ... passed on second and final reading. MOTION CARRIED, UNANIMOUS.' Differences from the record: the extension is Ordinance 2025-001, adopted 2025-01-07; the minutes give no term or end date; the original 2024 ordinance number was not found. Pasadena City Council imposed a commercial moratorium on permits for BESS facilities (City and ETJ) by Ordinance 2024-198: public hearings and first reading 2024-10-01, second and final reading at the 2024-10-08 special meeting (minutes). The extension ordinance recites that the moratorium expires 90 days after adoption unless extended, and Section 2 extends it once for a 90-day period past January 6, 2025; council minutes show it as Ordinance 2025-001, first reading 2025-01-06 and final reading 2025-01-07, unanimous (a first reading on 2024-12-17 was deferred). By its own terms the extension ran out in early April 2025 (90 days past January 6, 2025). On 2025-04-01 the council passed on final reading Ordinance 2025-082 adding Chapter 9, Article XII, Energy Storage Systems (first reading 2025-03-18), a permanent land use code for BESS that does not mention the moratorium. I found no further extension or new BESS moratorium: council minutes from 2025-01-21 through 2025-07-01 and 2025-11-18 have no BESS item, and page 2 (docketed public hearings, which a Texas ch. 212 moratorium or extension requires) of every council agenda from June 2025 through October 2026 lists no BESS hearing. The record's status extended/in_force and its claim that the moratorium is active and expires October 2026 are contradicted; the moratorium appears to have expired in April 2025 and been superseded by Ordinance 2025-082. The text of Ordinance 2024-198 itself was not read (the October 1, 2024 backup packet is a 762-page scan with no text layer); its date, scope and 90-day term are taken from the October 2024 minutes and the recitals of Ordinance 2025-001. The extension text read is the agenda-backup copy (number left blank, dated 12/10/24); the minutes confirm adoption under the same caption. Quoted: "WHEREAS, that the moratorium imposed by the City of Pasadena on the issuance of permits for the placement and installation of BESS facilities within the City relates to the preservation of the public peace, health, safety, and/or welfare of the citizens and following its adoption will expire 90 days therefrom, unless extended prior to that date after notice and hearing; ... WHEREAS, the City of Pasadena after a public hearing held on January 6, 2025 and January 7, 2025 to hear residents and affected parties on the proposed extension of the moratorium imposed on October 8, 2024, finds that extending the moratorium for a 90 day period effective from January 7, 2025, is necessary ... SECTION 2. That the City Council finds it is in the best interest of the City and does hereby extend the commercial moratorium imposed on the issuance of permits for the placement and installation of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) facilities within the jurisdiction of the City of Pasadena, Texas as established by Ordinance 2024-198 for a 90-day period past January 6, 2025." Second reading (agent:blind-reviewer-8 (Claude Code, 2026-10-16), opened): The document is the City of Pasadena ordinance (2025-001) that extended the BESS commercial moratorium imposed October 8, 2024 by Ordinance 2024-198, for a 90-day period past January 6, 2025; the January 6, 2025 minutes record first reading and the January 7, 2025 minutes record passage on second and final reading. Place, technology, type, scope and the 2024 enactment year agree. Status, currency and description do not: the extension ran only to about April 6, 2025. The council then passed Ordinance 2025-082 (new Chapter 9, Article XII, Energy Storage Systems) on first reading March 18, 2025 and final reading April 1, 2025, and the October 7, 2025 agenda backup carries an ordinance adopting the 2024 International Fire Code that repeals 2025-082 and moves the ESS requirements into the fire code. I read every City Council minutes file posted for 2025 (January 6 through July 1 and November 18), every 2025 and 2026 agenda backup with a text layer, the OCR of the scanned May 5 through October 6, 2026 agendas, and the October 20, 2026 agenda: none mentions a further moratorium extension, hearing or new BESS moratorium. Also read: Notice of Public Hearing for January 6, 2025 (Agenda/_01062025-549), minutes of October 1, 2024 (Minutes/_10012024-531) and October 8, 2024 (Minutes/_10082024-533), March 18, 2025 agenda backup (Agenda/_03182025-571), March 18 and April 1, 2025 minutes (Minutes/_03182025-570, Minutes/_04012025-574), October 7, 2025 agenda backup (Agenda/_10072025-629). The record's status should read expired (end about 2025-04-06), not extended and in force; the tracker claim of a moratorium expiring October 2026 is not supported by the council record.

Read the text of Ordinance 2025-205 in the City of Pasadena's Agenda Backup Documents for the October 7, 2025 council meeting (PDF pages 434 to 474; unsigned first-reading copy with the number left blank; a scan with an OCR text layer, and the operative pages were checked against the page images). It amends the Fire Prevention Code (Chapter 13, Article VII, Secs. 13-151 and 13-152) to adopt the 2024 International Fire Code with local amendments, and Section 3 repeals Ordinance 2025-082 (adopted April 1, 2025) in whole (Section 6 only preserves rights and remedies already accrued to the City), because 'requirements regarding energy storage systems' are being updated in the fire code. Section 9 delays the whole ordinance until 90 days after council approval. The minutes printed in the October 21 and November 4, 2025 agendas show first reading on 2025-10-07 and second and final reading on 2025-10-21, both unanimous, with no amendment recorded; the October 21 backup does not reprint the text. The Fire Marshal's Plan Review page says the code was adopted October 21, 2025 and 'took effect January 19, 2026'. So Chapter 9 Article XII stayed in force until the repeal took effect on 2026-01-19 and has stood repealed since; the record's status active and currency in_force are out of date (a repealed instrument is recorded as lifted under COUNTY_CHECK section 3). Much of Article XII moved into a new IFC Section 1208 in Exhibit A. Section 1208.4 Site Location keeps the five-acre cap (now 'excluding setbacks areas'), 1,500 ft between BESS sites, 1,000 ft from critical facilities (redefined: hospitals, nursing homes, police and fire stations, utilities, hazardous-material sites, water and wastewater plants; schools, day care centers and government facilities, listed in 2025-082, are no longer named), 50 ft from the right of way, 150 ft from rear and side property lines (no longer limited to lines adjoining commercial property), no special flood hazard area, and frontage on a public right of way. Section 1208.3 still requires a Special Use Permit application and CenterPoint Energy review and approval before a city permit. Not carried over: the 500 ft setback from residential property, multifamily developments and manufactured home parks; the rule that a site lie within 150 ft of CenterPoint property; and the plume study. Section 1201.4 states land-use aims ('designation of properties suitable for the location' of a BESS; 'compatible land uses'), but the vehicle is the fire code, so whether Section 1208.4 counts under COUNTY_CHECK section 3 is a decision for the record-editor; its size cap and distances are local siting rules, not IFC clearances. No later council action on energy storage was found: the main council agendas from November 4, 2025 through October 6, 2026 (23 agendas, OCR'd here, carrying the minutes of the meetings before them) name no energy storage, battery, Article XII or Section 13-152 item, and AgendaCenter phrase searches after 2025-10-22 for energy storage, battery energy, fire code, Article XII, 13-152 and 1208 return no results (that index missed the October 7, 2025 backup, so it is not conclusive alone). Ordinance 2026-118 (final reading 2026-07-21) changes only the Section 13-12 fee schedule and names no BESS fee. Quoted: "WHEREAS, it is also recommended that Ordinance 2025-082, adopted on April 1, 2025, be repealed, as requirements regarding energy storage systems is being updated by adoption of this Ordinance; NOW THEREFORE, ... SECTION 3. That Ordinance 2025-082, previously adopted by Council on April 1, 2025 is hereby repealed. ... SECTION 9. That the provisions of this Ordinance shall not take effect until ninety (90) days after Council approval of this Ordinance, such ninety (90) day grace period from the date of adoption until implementation to allow the construction industry to conform." Replacing text, Exhibit A new IFC Sec. 1208 (1208.4 Site Location names solar PV arrays, energy storage systems and dedicated-use buildings): kept are the five-acre cap (1208.4(a), now excluding setback areas), 1,000 ft from critical facilities (1208.4(d); the new Sec. 1202.1 critical facility definition is flood-oriented and no longer lists schools, day care centers or government facilities), 1,500 ft between BESS sites (1208.4(c)), no special flood hazard area (1208.4(f)) and the Special Use Permit application (1208.3 item 4; 1208.4.3). Resolution 2026-6 (adopted 2026-02-17, effective immediately) replaces the county's solar regulations with amended Solar Energy Facility Regulations for facilities of 1 MW or more, by Special Use Permit in the Agricultural zone. The current setback table keeps 70 feet from property lines, power or communication lines and roads or railroads, but sets 500 feet from occupied structures, not the 300 feet in the record; the Board may waive or tighten any setback case by case. It also adds a 1:8 footprint ratio, an 80-acre footprint cap per section and a 1/4 mile (1,320 feet) scenic highway setback. Item 4 rescinds the community solar moratorium of Resolution 2025-25. The record's 2023 values probably come from the original 2023 regulations (Resolution 2023-27 on the 2023-08-29 agenda per search results), which the reader could not open: the old county site returns 403 and the Internet Archive was unreachable, so whether 2023 said 300 feet is unconfirmed. The official copy is a 28-page recorded scan read by OCR (RapidOCR); its text matches a typed copy of the same regulations posted by Colorado Counties Inc. (ccionline.org, Solar-Regulations.Logan-2-19-2026.pdf), which was used only to cross-check the OCR. Quoted: "2. Setbacks. Unless otherwise required by federal or state regulations applicable to the Solar Energy Facility, the following minimum setbacks shall apply. ... Setback from above-ground public electric power lines or communication lines. 70 feet ... Setback from existing public road or highway or railroad. 70 feet ... Setback from occupied structures including: residence, school, hospital, church or public library, unless appropriate easements are secured. 500 feet ... Setback from all other property lines 70 feet ... e. All setbacks may be waived or made more restrictive by the Board of County Commissioners on a case-by-case basis." Second reading (agent:blind-reviewer-6 (Claude Code, 2026-10-19), opened): Resolution 2026-6 amends the Logan County Zoning Resolution by adopting amended Solar Energy Facility Regulations, effective February 17, 2026; it also rescinds the solar moratorium set by Resolution 2025-25 and keeps solar a use by special permit in the Agricultural Zone. The record's NREL compilation dates to 2023 (its ordinance_url names Resolution 2023-27), so this is a later amendment of the record's instrument. The amended Safety Setbacks table sets 70 feet from all other property lines (agrees with the record), 70 feet from public roads, railroads and above-ground power or communication lines, and 500 feet from occupied structures unless easements are secured (the record says 300 feet). Section 1-106(A)(8) also places the facility 500 feet from any occupied structure or water well, and Section 1-106(B)(3) sets a 1/4 mile (1,320 feet) scenic highway setback. Setbacks may be waived or made more restrictive by the Board case by case. The regulations also cap the above ground footprint (1 to 8 encumbrance ratio, 80 acres per section) and set a noise limit. The 2023-27 copy at the record's ordinance_url returned HTTP 403 and was not read, so whether 300 feet was the 2023 value could not be checked. Resolution 2026-11 (adopted April 7, 2026, effective immediately) replaces the county's wind regulations with amended Wind Energy Regulations in the Zoning Resolution, for wind facilities of 1 MW or more by special use permit in the Agricultural zone. Its setbacks, measured from the tower center, are 1.5 times tip height from public power or communication lines and from public roads, highways and railroads, 2.5 times tip height from occupied structures, 1 times tip height from non-participating property boundaries, and 1/4 mile (1320 feet) from designated scenic highways; the Board may reduce or waive setbacks. Shadow flicker must be under 1 hour a year on average at occupied structures. Noise follows C.R.S. 25-12-103, capped at light industrial levels at the receiving property. The Wind Energy Regulations, as amended, shall remain in effect until further amendment or repeal by the Board of County Commissioners. ... Setback from above-ground public electric power lines or communication lines. 1.5 Times Tip Height. Setback from existing public road or highway or railroad. 1.5 Times Tip Height. Setback from occupied structures including: residence, school, hospital, church or public library, unless appropriate easements are secured. 2.5 Times Tip Height. Setback from non-participating1 landowner property boundaries. 1 Times Tip Height. 1 Non-participating means not within the project boundary. [1-106(A)(11)(c)(vi)] The Wind Energy Facility shall be designed in a manner to result in less than one (1) hour annually, on average, of shadow flicker caused by project components, measured at the central point of any occupied structures." The record's ban/prohibition type and mechanism are not supported: the section contains no prohibition of wind projects, and the 330 cap is a county-wide limit on total turbines. The section also sets a 30 minute per day flicker limit, 75 foot minimum blade clearance, a two mile maximum spacing between turbines in a project, 300 foot setbacks from open ditches and tile, a 120% setback from roads, and owner waivers, which the record does not mention. Setbacks are measured from the tower center point to the dwelling or building, and to the property line for other areas. The file states no ordinance number or adoption date, so the date and status remain unverified; the minutes that adopted it were not located. Quoted: "70.07 WIND ENERGY CONVERSION SYSTEMS. Two record values are not supported. The document does not date the enactment of Section 561; it lists readoptions through 2026-01-20 including 2023-01-10, so the record's 2023 is not confirmed. My first draft wrongly marked both as agreeing. Also note: applies to systems under 5 MW, conditional use permit in all districts, and the resolution covers unincorporated land not under township zoning (561 text read; Blendon and other townships with their own zoning are outside it). Quoted: "SECTION 561.04 ... b) Tower: 1) The tower of a tower-mounted wind energy system shall not exceed 150 feet in height. ... c) Sound Level: 1) Operation of wind energy systems shall not exceed 55 decibels, except during short-term events such as severe wind storms and utility outages. ... all readings, if necessary, shall be taken from the nearest neighboring property line. d) Shadow Flicker: 1) Wind energy systems shall be sited in a manner that does not result in shadow flicker impacts. The applicant has the burden of proving that their wind energy system does not have an impact on neighboring or adjacent uses either through siting or mitigation. a) Fall Zone 1) A tower mounted wind energy system shall have a fall zone at least 110% of the total height from: a. Second reading (agent:blind-reviewer-11 (Claude Code, 2026-10-26), opened): Height, noise, setback/fall zone, state, jurisdiction, technology and status agree. Two fields do not match the document: the shadow flicker rule has no numeric hours per year (it requires siting that avoids shadow flicker impacts, applicant proves it), and no enactment date for Section 561 can be read from the document (cover list shows readoptions through January 20, 2026, including January 10, 2023, so the record's 2023 is not confirmed). Also, the setback is a fall zone, with property-line waiver by recorded easement, and the system must be under 5 MW. Wind systems are conditional uses in all districts (561.03).
